family: Convexity / long-volatility replication by dynamic trading on spot (trend-as-lookback-straddle, breakout/range tactics, gamma-scalping analogues without options, crash alpha, variance-ratio-gated switching between a trend book and a reversal book)
thesis: A threshold-rebalanced long/short trend rule is a dynamically replicated long straddle: over a window of T days its gross P&L decomposes exactly (Dao et al. 2016, eq. 7) into (λ/2)(S_T − S_0)² − (λ/2)Σ D_t², i.e. it RECEIVES the long-horizon variance (the straddle payoff; the capped sign rule gives the V-shaped |S_T − S_0| payoff, Fung–Hsieh's lookback version is S_max − S_min) and PAYS the short-horizon realised variance as a running premium, which is what whipsaw losses in ranges are. Its expectation is (λT/2)σ₁²(VR(T) − 1): positive only if the Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio at the trend scale exceeds 1 (Hurst H > 1/2, positive summed autocorrelation). That is a bet on the return distribution's second-order structure, not free convexity, and the operator's repo already measures the failure of exactly this bet: the 819 book's PIT gross Sharpe went +1.22 (BEAR22) → +0.13 (BULL24) → +0.22 (CHOP25) with net@21 +1.06 → −0.15 → +0.02 (`runs/819_single_asset/POWERED_RESULT.md:48-57`), and the 21 bp cost drag is only 0.15–0.28 Sharpe-points per regime — the premium (whipsaw inside gross) is what consumed the payoff, not the fee. The reversal book is the same object with the sign flipped (a short straddle: collects short-term variance, pays long-term variance, positive iff VR < 1); a VR-gated switch between them is a forecast of the persistence of the autocorrelation regime; crash alpha via drawdown-conditional shorting is a conditional-mean forecast dressed as a tactic. Under the no-free-lunch discipline the profit source is therefore MIXED: predominantly a forecast (of VR(τ) − 1, i.e. distributional/autocorrelation structure rather than the mean), with the only genuinely forecast-free component in the family being the constant-mix rebalancing premium ≈ ½(σ̄_i² − σ_p²) ≈ 10–13 %/yr gross on this universe minus ≈3 %/yr at 21 bp, which is long-only, beta-one, relative to B&H and therefore fails BEAR-positivity by construction (B&H BEAR22 −2.54). No risk premium is available: nobody on Kraken spot pays a premium to be hedged by this book. Cost reduction is second-order at daily turnover 0.15/day. The record has never measured the one quantity the family stands or falls on — whether VR at the trend scale is PERSISTENT across windows on the daily PIT panel — and that measurement is cheap (CPU-hours).
math: Core identities (Dao–Nguyen–Deremble–Lempérière–Bouchaud–Potters 2016, read in full): position Π_t = λ(S_t − S_0) ⇒ G_T = Σ_t Π_{t−1}D_t = (λ/2)(S_T − S_0)² − (λ/2)Σ_{t≤T} D_t² (eq. 7); ⟨G_T⟩ = (λT/2)(σ²(T) − σ²(1)) (eq. 8) with the signature plot σ²(τ) = σ² + (2/τ)Σ_{u=1}^{τ}(τ − u)C(u) (eq. 4). Hence ⟨G_T⟩ = (λT/2)σ₁²·(VR(T) − 1), VR(T) := σ²(T)/σ²(1) = Var(Σ of T obs)/(T·Var(1 obs)) — literally the statistic in `experiments/901_range_based_dependence_probe/range_probe.py:218-240` (`variance_ratio(x,q)` = Var(sum of q consecutive obs)/(q·Var(1 obs)), overlapping, no small-sample df correction). Fractional-Brownian reading: VR(T) ≈ T^{2H−1} ⇒ ⟨G⟩ > 0 ⟺ H > 1/2. Capped ±1 sign rule (the 819 form, `trader/strategy.py:60-77`): ⟨G|𝒯⟩ = λτ(|𝒯| − √(2/π)) (eq. 15) with 𝒯 the vol-normalised τ-day trend; with 𝒯 ~ N(0, VR(τ)), E|𝒯| = √(2VR/π) ⇒ ⟨G⟩ = λτ√(2/π)(√VR(τ) − 1). Reversal book = −sign(𝒯) ⇒ ⟨G⟩ = −λτ√(2/π)(√VR(τ) − 1) > 0 ⟺ VR(τ) < 1. Add proportional cost c on turnover: ⟨net⟩ = λτ√(2/π)(√VR(τ) − 1) − c·E[turnover]. Annualised per-asset gross Sharpe of the sign rule (Gaussian, τ-window aggregation, sd ≈ λ√τ): S ≈ √365·√(2/π)·(√VR(τ) − 1) ≈ 15.2·(√VR(τ) − 1). Break-even against the measured 21 bp drag: 819 PIT FULL turn 0.152/day → 55.5×/yr → 11.65 %/yr @21 bp (`POWERED_RESULT.md:88`); FULL gross +0.74 vs net@21 +0.56 ⇒ drag 0.18 Sharpe ⇒ implied book vol ≈ 11.65/0.18 ≈ 65 %/yr (≈3.4 %/day); √VR − 1 ≥ 0.18/15.2 = 0.012 ⇒ VR(30) ≥ ≈1.024 is all the fee requires. The rule's 2024–25 gross of +0.13/+0.22 therefore says VR(30) ≈ 1.00–1.02 on this panel in those years — the premium ate the payoff; the fee is second-order (consistent with the Economies-2026 finding that daily BTC VR ≈ 1, 2013→2026-02). Estimation noise of the gate (Lo–MacKinlay iid asymptotics): sd[VR(q)] ≈ √(2(2q−1)(q−1)/(3qn)); q = 30, n = 180 → 0.46; q = 5, n = 180 → 0.16; pooled over N_eff ≈ 8 assets → ≈0.06 at q = 5 — i.e. 5–40× the break-even margin of 0.02, so a per-asset daily VR gate cannot resolve the sign of VR − 1 unless regime swings are large (≈0.7 vs 1.3), which is exactly the persistence question the record has never measured. Cost arithmetic to respect: 0.155·21 bp = 3.26 bp/day = 11.9 %/yr; a gate flip costs 2/n per asset (full book flip = 2·gross·21 bp = 42 bp ≈ 0.6 % of a 65 %-vol book's daily sd) — bounded and small with hysteresis. Rebalancing premium (the one forecast-free term): ½(σ̄² − σ_p²) with σ_i ≈ 0.8, ρ̄ ≈ 0.6, N = 64 ⇒ σ_p² ≈ 0.388 ⇒ ≈ 12.6 %/yr gross vs B&H, turnover ≈ Σ|Δw| ≈ σ_daily·√(2(1−ρ)) ≈ 0.038/day ⇒ 2.9 %/yr @21 bp ⇒ ≈ +0.15 Sharpe relative to a long-only B&H that read −2.54 in BEAR22 — real, small, not bear-positive.

bear_positive_without_forecast.argument: Structurally, a long-convexity (trend) book is the only member of this panel that is positive in a bear WITHOUT a directional forecast, because (S_T − S_0)² is sign-agnostic — but only when the bear is a slow trend at scale ≥ τ and only after the whipsaw premium has been paid in the ranges around it. The record shows both halves. BEAR22 (2021-11-10→2022-12-31, BTC −77 % over 12 months, BTC daily vol 3.34 % ≈ 64 %/yr annualised): 819 PIT gross +1.22, net@21 +1.06 vs B&H −2.54 (`POWERED_RESULT.md:53`); real ohlcv_daily baseline BEAR22 +1.095 vs long-flat variant −2.471 (LEDGER `898/trend-decay`) — the short side WAS the crash alpha. 2026H1 bear (B&H −2.45/−2.61): baseline −1.659 CI[−5.30,+0.95] (898); 820 gate 2 unseen 2025-12-13→2026-07-04 gross −1.18, net@8 −1.31 (`tasks/TASK_820_SHIP_TREND_CTA.md:111-114`) — beats B&H by ≈1.3 Sharpe but is absolute-negative: a bear whose legs were faster than the 30-day trend scale, exactly Dao et al. §2.6/§5 ('no protection against moves on time scales ≪ τ'). The premium: BULL24 gross +0.13 / net@21 −0.15, CHOP25 +0.22 / +0.02 with BTC daily vol falling 2.80 % (2024) → 2.24 % (2025, K33: lowest on record) — lower vol shrinks (S_T − S_0)² faster than it shrinks the fee-plus-whipsaw bill. So: BEAR-positive is CONDITIONAL on VR(τ) > 1 inside the bear window (true 2022, false 2026H1), and the 'without forecast' clause fails in the strict sense — the payoff's expectation is (λT/2)σ₁²(VR(T) − 1), a bet on autocorrelation; the goalposts also demand the ABSOLUTE bar (+0.97 net@21 on unseen years), and 'beats B&H in the bear' is what 898 explicitly records as a crash-hedge property, not an edge. Crash alpha via drawdown-conditional shorting (candidate c) is a conditional-mean forecast (that drawdowns continue) — HRVH's no-long restriction raised worst-quintile return ≈26 % → ≈33 % while lowering the average (Fig. 7, p. 14-15: 'the price one pays'), and its crypto analogue (short-or-flat) has never been measured here; 898 measured long-flat only.

literature.ref: Dao, T.-L., Nguyen, T.-T., Deremble, C., Lempérière, Y., Bouchaud, J.-P., Potters, M. (2016) 'Tail protection for long investors: Trend convexity at work', arXiv:1607.02410
literature.claim: Trend P&L = long-term realised variance minus short-term realised variance (the whipsaw premium); positive iff long-horizon vol > short-horizon vol (VR > 1); capped sign rule gives a V-shaped payoff; no protection against moves faster than the trend/rebalance scale; a trend is a strangle portfolio that pays realised short-term variance instead of implied variance.
literature.numbers: Eq. 7: G_T = (λ/2)(S_T−S_0)² − (λ/2)ΣD_t²; eq. 8: ⟨ΣG⟩ = (λT/2)(σ²(T) − σ²(1)); eq. 4 signature plot; eq. 11: ⟨G|𝒯⟩ = (λτ/2)(𝒯² − 1); eq. 15 (sign rule): ⟨G|𝒯⟩ = λτ(|𝒯| − √(2/π)). §3: EMA replicator τ = 180 d correlates > 80 % with SG CTA Index 2000–2015 with 2 % costs + 1/20 fees (Fig. 7-8); convexity of SG CTA vs S&P: R² 0.02 on monthly returns → 0.18–0.2 when aggregated at τ' ≈ 90 d against a 180-d trend (Fig. 9). §4.3: 'long-vol portfolios have consistently lost money over the past 2 decades' while trend was positive — the premium is cheaper via trend because it is realised short-term variance, not implied. §2.6: 'blind to moves on time scales ≪ τ'.

controllability: Hold on policy is this family's genuine strength and the reason it is worth one cheap row. Action space: per asset {−w_i, 0, +w_i} with w_i = 1/n_present (`trader/strategy.py:123-135`), i.e. 3^N books collapsed by the rule to a deterministic function of closes; the whole policy is 3–4 parameters (trend lookback L, VR horizon q, VR window n, hysteresis band) plus the frozen 819 constants. Auditability: every position is reproducible from `trader.strategy.build_positions` on a close panel; the gate state is a scalar per asset (or one per market) that can be logged and eyeballed; positions never depend on a learned object. Bounded turnover: the sign rule turns 0.146–0.180/day of gross (`POWERED_RESULT.md:48-57`); a regime switch costs one book flip (2·gross → 42 bp at 21 bp, ≈0.6 % of a 65 %-vol book's daily sd); with hysteresis ±0.1 on VR̂ and a minimum dwell of q days, gate flips are capped at ≈365/q per year per asset, so worst-case extra cost ≈ (365/q)·42 bp ≈ 3 %/yr at q = 5 and ≈0.5 %/yr at q = 30. Risk control composes: the shipped `RiskConfig` shadow-scale drawdown throttle (`trader/config.py:113-127`) halves gross at −20 % and scales to 0.25 at −35 % without a dead state, measured to cut maxDD −37.8 % → −32.2 % on unseen data (`TASK_820:114-115`). What is lost: (1) any continuous-forecast edge — the book cannot size on conviction, so Grinold–Kahn breadth is spent as sign-only bets (Dao eq. 15: the V-shaped payoff loses the parabola's 𝒯² gain on large trends); (2) the gate parameter IS the bet — choosing q and the threshold is choosing which autocorrelation regime you believe persists, and a pre-registered grid of ~16 cells buys a Bonferroni haircut; (3) a range-based vol-stop (Parkinson/YZ on true daily H/L) reintroduces a shorter-scale trend rule inside the reversal book, i.e. a second premium; (4) the rebalancing-premium sub-family is controllable but beta-one and fails BEAR-positivity by construction.

kill_experiment.design: Pre-registered, PIT, by-year, net@21, fixed grid, no fitting. Arms: A0 = ungated 819 trend book (frozen `trader.config.STRATEGY`, the control); A1 = ungated reversal book (−sign(logc_t − logc_{t−L}), L ∈ {3, 7}); A2 = market-level VR gate: VR̂_t(q) computed by `range_probe.variance_ratio` on the trailing n days of the equal-weight PIT market log-return, q ∈ {5, 10}, n ∈ {180, 365}, state = trend if VR̂ > 1+h, reversal if VR̂ < 1−h, flat otherwise, h = 0.10, minimum dwell q days — 4 cells; A3 = same gate per asset — 4 cells; A4 = placebo for every A2/A3 cell: the gate-state sequence circularly shifted by ≥ 365 days (block-preserving, destroys alignment); A5 = A0 with a range-based vol-stop (flat an asset when 5-d Parkinson vol from true daily H/L via `read_ohlcv_daily` exceeds 2× its trailing 60-d value) — 1 cell, tests the HRVH 'restriction' analogue on spot. Universe = 819 POWERED PIT builder (`trader.data.build_pit_universe`, 273 assets, dead coins in); panel = true UTC daily bars (`aggregate_asset_daily` / `ohlcv_daily`, not the minute stride); windows = calendar 2021…2025, 2026H1, BEAR22, FULL, with 2024-01→2026-06 the graded unseen span. Mandatory diagnostic regardless of verdict: the lag-1 autocorrelation of market-level VR̂(q) across NON-overlapping n-day windows with a block-bootstrap CI — the 'is the autocorrelation regime persistent' number the whole family rests on — plus the per-year distribution of per-asset VR̂ with its iid sd √(2(2q−1)(q−1)/(3qn)) printed alongside so noise is not read as regime. SPEC ≤ 1 page, sha256 recorded before the first run; the grid is frozen; anything added later is a new row.
kill_experiment.instrument: Unmodified `trader.backtest.window_metrics` (backtest.py:328-372) and `cell_metrics` (:231-283), seed 819, n_boot 2000, tiers 8/21, gates via `clears_gate`/`bear_positive` (:285-301); positions from `trader.strategy.build_positions` (strategy.py:137-155) with the gate applied as a mask on `sig` before `pos = w * sig`; VR from `experiments/901_range_based_dependence_probe/range_probe.py:218-240`; new module `experiments/9xx_vr_gate/` (runner + SPEC only), epoch named and PIT frame pinned per `LEDGER.md:28-41`; shares TASK_915's panel and the 899 daily-ingest precondition.
kill_experiment.pass_fail: PASS: some A2/A3 cell on PIT 2024-01→2026-06 has net@21 ≥ +0.97 with block-bootstrap CI lo > 0, beats BOTH A0 and A1 net@21 in each of 2024, 2025, 2026H1 separately, is BEAR22-positive and beats B&H there (form check), holds positions (median gross ≥ 0.5, no > 95 %-flat days), survives Bonferroni over the 8 gated cells, AND its A4 placebo does not also clear — then hand it to the gate ladder. MARGINAL: same with ≥ +0.56 only (record, do not ship). FAIL: anything else — including the case where the gated cell beats A0 but not A1 or vice versa (that is regime luck, not a switch). Pre-committed consequences: FAIL closes convexity/long-vol tactics on the daily Kraken surface as a family (no further breakout/range/VR-switch rows); the VR̂ diagnostic and the reversal signal are handed to TASK_915 as F1/F2 features to be IC-tested, not gated; a positive VR-persistence diagnostic with a FAIL on the book is recorded as 'regime exists, not harvestable at 21 bp' with the measured margin. Kill date 10 days from SPEC commit.
kill_experiment.cost: < 2 CPU-hours of compute on gpu-server under safe_run; 1–2 agent-days to author SPEC + runner + smoke on the fixture; zero GPU; no new data beyond the 899 daily ingest already required by 915.

honest_odds: P(a convexity tactic clears the goalposts — PIT, unseen 2024-01→2026-06, fee16/slip5, net@21 ≥ +0.97, CI lo > 0, BEAR-positive, holds positions) ≈ 3–5 %; P(≥ +0.56 marginal) ≈ 8–10 %; P(the VR-persistence diagnostic is statistically nonzero at market level, which would make the row worth having run for 915's sake) ≈ 30–40 %. Reasoning: (1) the payoff's expectation is (λT/2)σ₁²(VR(T) − 1) and the repo's own gross numbers say VR(30) ≈ 1.00–1.02 on this panel in 2024–25 (gross +0.13/+0.22, `POWERED_RESULT.md:55-56`), corroborated externally by daily BTC VR ≈ 1 over 2013→2026-02 (Economies 2026) and an R/S Hurst of 0.56 that is bias-equivalent to 0.5; (2) the gate must forecast the sign of VR − 1 one window ahead, and per-asset VR̂ has iid sd 0.16–0.46 for q = 5–30 at n = 180 — 5–40× the 0.02 break-even margin — so only large, persistent regime swings could be harvested, and nothing in the record suggests they exist at daily scale; (3) the cost is second-order (0.15–0.28 Sharpe drag at 21 bp) so the fee-tier argument cannot rescue or kill it — the premium does; (4) 813's 132 intraday trigger cells dissolved and 898's variants are dead, which is exactly what a VR ≈ 1 surface produces; (5) the one clean bear win (BEAR22 +1.22 gross) is a slow 12-month trend at 64 %/yr vol, and the two recent bear-shaped windows (820 gate 2, 2026H1) were fast and read negative, while vol has compressed to 43 %/yr — the (S_T − S_0)² term is shrinking faster than the premium. Why still run it: it is the cheapest row in the panel, its FAIL branch closes an entire family that would otherwise keep re-proposing itself, and its diagnostic (VR persistence on the daily PIT panel) is a number 915 needs anyway.
open_doubts: The break-even arithmetic uses Dao et al.'s Gaussian, constant-normalised-vol toy model; crypto's vol clustering and fat tails change the constant 15.2 and the sd of VR̂ — the diagnostic arm should print empirical (block-bootstrap) sd of VR̂, not the iid formula.

Implied book vol ≈ 65 %/yr is back-solved from the gross-vs-net@21 Sharpe gap on the PIT table; the 898 real-data JSON (`runs/898_decay_trading_data.json` / srv `experiments/898_trend_decay/results/decay_trading_data.json`) is not on the workstation, so the 2024–26 gross and turnover per year were not read first-hand — only net@8 from the LEDGER row.

Whether market-level VR persistence exists at daily scale on Kraken has never been measured here; the 901 instrument's own history (VR over-certifies at 0.185 on φ=.999; read-off rules flipped verdicts across three cycles) says any VR-based gate needs an SE-aware threshold, not a fixed one.

A short-or-flat crash-alpha variant (HRVH's no-long restriction, spot-margin-legal in the env) has never been measured; 898 measured long-flat and lev-matched only. It cannot clear the absolute bar alone (negative expectation in bulls by construction) but would quantify the crypto 'bond-smile' analogue.

The 21 bp tier is applied as one-sided proportional cost on turnover; the 907 probe's adverse-selection estimate could move the 2/n book-flip cost by ±5 bp per side — second-order for this family (≈0.03 Sharpe on the gate's flips), but should be stated in the SPEC.

Bonferroni over 8 gated cells is the pre-registered correction; if the planner widens the grid (more q, n, h) the multiplicity haircut grows and the 3–5 % odds fall further — the grid must be fixed before the first run.

Rebalancing-premium arithmetic (≈ +0.15 Sharpe relative to B&H at 21 bp) uses assumed σ_i ≈ 0.8, ρ̄ ≈ 0.6; the actual PIT panel's dispersion and correlation were not computed here (read-only consult).

External crypto trend claims (arXiv 2602.11708 Sharpe 2.41; Zarattini et al. > 1.5 net) were read at abstract level only, with undisclosed cost assumptions in the first and no 2022 breakdown in either — neither is citable against the goalposts.
